title: Understanding Ali's Quiet Courage
script: Narrator: [thoughtful] People often ask why Ali ibn Abi Talib is remembered so strongly for courage, even among many brave companions.
Narrator: [reflective] I want to share one night from his life that I think explains it better than any list of qualities.
Narrator: [serious] Enemies in Makkah had finally agreed on a terrible plan, to attack the Prophet together, inside his own home, at night.
Narrator: [calm] Warned in advance, the Prophet needed to leave the city quietly, without anyone noticing his absence until it was too late.
Narrator: [warmly] But someone needed to remain behind, lying in his bed, to make the enemies believe he was still sleeping there.
Narrator: [with admiration] Ali agreed immediately, without asking for time to think it over or weighing the danger to himself.
Narrator: [tense] That night, armed men surrounded the house, watching closely, waiting for the right moment to enter and strike.
Narrator: [calm] Ali lay there in the darkness, knowing full well that the men outside might discover the truth at any moment.
Narrator: [reflective] He did not know, lying there, whether he would survive until morning. Yet he stayed completely still and calm.
Narrator: [with wonder] When morning came, the enemies finally entered and were shocked to find Ali instead of the Prophet they expected.
Narrator: [calm] By then, the Prophet was already safely on his way toward Madinah, exactly as they had carefully planned together.
Narrator: [thoughtful] What strikes me most isn't only the danger Ali faced, but the complete absence of hesitation in his decision.
Narrator: [warmly] He didn't need applause or recognition. He simply loved the Prophet and trusted Allah more than he feared death.
Narrator: [reflective] Later in his life, Ali became known for his wisdom, his fairness as a judge, and eventually as caliph.
Narrator: [peacefully] But whenever his name comes up, I always return first to that quiet, dangerous night, and his stillness inside it.
Narrator: [warmly] Real courage, I've learned from his story, often looks less like a loud battle and more like quiet, steady trust.

quiz.question: What plan had the enemies in Makkah agreed on?
options: To attack the Prophet inside his own home at night
To hold a meeting with him
quiz.explanation: Enemies had agreed on a plan to attack the Prophet together, inside his own home, at night.

quiz.question: What did Ali agree to do that night?
options: Lie in the Prophet's bed to make enemies believe he was still there
quiz.explanation: Ali agreed to remain behind, lying in the Prophet's bed, so the enemies would believe he was still sleeping there.

quiz.question: How did Ali react when asked to take this risk?
options: He hesitated for a long time
He agreed immediately, without asking for time to think it over
He asked someone else to do it
quiz.explanation: Ali agreed immediately, without asking for time to think it over or weighing the danger to himself.

quiz.question: What happened when the enemies entered in the morning?
options: They were shocked to find Ali instead of the Prophet
quiz.explanation: When morning came, the enemies were shocked to find Ali instead of the Prophet they expected.

quiz.question: What does the narrator conclude real courage often looks like?
quiz.explanation: The narrator concludes that real courage often looks less like a loud battle and more like quiet, steady trust.
